resolutions.title: Fresh explore-to-propose changes are forced onto the unattached path
resolutions.action: Rekeyed the generation-input precondition on TRACKED state in the shared reference (PR_PROPOSE_SECTION): the skip fires only when `orbit/explore/<change-name>/` is tracked in HEAD (`git ls-files --error-unmatch`) AND absent-or-different on the target ref (`git diff --quiet HEAD <target> -- <dir>`), on BOTH the reuse and the create path; an UNTRACKED exploration — the ordinary state, since explore commits nothing — never triggers it, and the one case git would refuse surfaces as the switch-failure skip. The delta requirement (orbit-propose-modifications) now says the same, its existing scenario covers absent-or-different, and a new scenario `An uncommitted exploration does not trigger the skip` names the untracked case on both target kinds; the tasks.md restatement (task 1.x phase list) aligned. Transcription: `generationInputGuard` hoisted ahead of BOTH switch paths in phase1.ts with the tracked-and-differs predicate. Harness: three new cases — untracked on the reuse path proceeds with the exploration intact, untracked on the create path proceeds, tracked-but-different on the target skips with HEAD unmoved and the newer content preserved (31/31). Propose and ff function-payload parity hashes re-pinned (SKILL.md content hashes unchanged — only the reference moved). Both external reviewers (Codex and the clean-context Fable pass) reached this finding independently by the same real-git experiment; the clean-context file's copy will suppress as stale on its walk.

resolutions.action: The reader now treats a present null as PRESENT-but-empty: `Empty 'pr' field in config: the key is present with no value (expected never | per-proposal | per-architecture); treating as 'never'` — only a genuinely absent key is silent. The comment that rationalized the silence is replaced. The test that codified it (`treats a bare pr: with no value as absent, silently`) now asserts exactly one warning containing `Empty 'pr' field` and `treating as 'never'`. The orbit-pr-lifecycle delta's config requirement gained the present-but-empty clause and a scenario `Present-but-empty config key warns`; the absent-key scenario is untouched. Chose A because the reader's job is to enforce the closed set once so the bodies never re-derive it, and a blank key is the malformation most likely to be an accident.
